title: Republic of China Minguo Calendar
intro: The Minguo or Republic of China calendar uses ordinary Gregorian months and days but numbers years from the founding of the Republic of China.
summary: Twelve Gregorian months; 1912 is Minguo year 1. The year 2026 is Minguo year 115.
origin: Republic of China era numbering begins in 1912. The convention is particularly familiar on dates and official records in Taiwan.
diagram_title: THE YEAR WITH A NEW NUMBER
structure: Month lengths and leap-day rules are the same as in the Gregorian calendar. Only the year label changes.
pattern_note: A Minguo year can be found by subtracting 1911 from a Gregorian year for dates from 1912 onward.
history: The Republic of China established a new national era count in 1912. Both Gregorian and Minguo labels may be encountered in records from Taiwan.
example: 15 June 2026 in Gregorian notation is 15 June Minguo 115. The month, day and weekday are unchanged.
limits: This is era-year notation, not a separate lunar month system. Retrospective labels for years before the Republic should not be mistaken for historical official dates.
